title: Midshift batch-fix log — Ling
content:
Goal: quick log of the midshift incident + experiment notes and next-step checklist. Keep short, actionable, and copyable into a PR/bug report.

What I saw (13:00–15:30):
- After the micro-batcher change rolled at ~12:50, p50 stable but p99 climbed from ~230ms -> ~780ms on gpu-pool-3 for short-seq workloads (seq_len<=128).
- CPU side queues show occasional bursts where a single request path holds the KV lock for ~150ms. Observed correlation between long lock holds and background async-eviction kicks.
- Ambient CPU at ~72%, GPU util ~55%. No obvious hardware throttling.
- Error rate low, but tail tokens drop slightly (~0.4% increase in 5xx) when p99 spikes.

What I tried / experiments run (quick notes):
1) Revert micro-batcher sampler to previous algo on canary (svc:rt-canary-2). Result: immediate reduction in p99 to ~250ms for the canary.
2) Heap snapshot of KV manager: free list shows churn tied to prefix-caching TTLs (defaults 60s). Bumping to 120s in test decreased eviction frequency.
3) Added lightweight tracing around kv_lock acquire/release (flag: enable_kv_tracing). Dumped ~1500 traces to s3://rt-debug/midshift/ for closer look.
4) Small quick patch: reduce contention by switching try_lock backoff to exponential (PR linked above). Deployed to staging only — no regressions observed in throughput.

Immediate hypothesis:
- Micro-batcher change increases the chance of longer-lived requests touching KV concurrently; combined with eager eviction (TTL 60s) causes more frequent cache reinsertions and lock contention, which manifests as p99 spikes for short requests.

Quick measurement artifacts to attach when filing bug:
- p99 timeline chart (13:00–16:00) from datadog: rtt_p99_per_pool.png
- kv_lock histograms pre/post (in traces)
- flamegraph of CPU around 13:40 (rt-canary-2)

Short TODO (order matters):
- [ ] Roll micro-batcher revert to canary -> monitor for 1h (Riley)
- [ ] Add e2e synthetic with sequence=64 steady load (100rps) to reproduce locally (me)
- [ ] Surface per-request kv cache hits in console for the pool (short-term metric) (Noah)
- [ ] Create regression test that simulates concurrent prefix-cache churn (me/Riley)
- [ ] Evaluate TTL bump impact at scale — ambient mem delta estimate: +12% mem per pool (quick calc) -> ops check (Noah)
- [ ] If revert holds, prepare a PR that reworks the micro-batcher sampling (not revert) to reduce concurrent hot-key collisions (me)

Notes to self / stray thoughts:
- Could we opportunistically prefetch KV for likely-next-prefix when batcher groups similar prefixes? Maybe a heuristic: if batcher groups >3 reqs with same prefix hint, prewarm.
- TTL 60s chosen historically for mem pressure; but modern workloads have more short-lived prefix reuse, so 120s might be net win. Need controlled A/B.
- Add a 'kv_lock_wait' metric with tag "eviction-in-progress" so we can correlate without full tracing.

Commands I used (copy for reproducer):
- dd/collect traces: ./bin/rt-trace-dump --svc rt-canary-2 --out s3://rt-debug/midshift/trace-$(date +%s).json --filter "kv_lock"
- quick local repro (docker): docker-compose -f docker-compose.local.yml run --rm loadgen ./loadgen --rps 100 --seq 64 --duration 600 --target http://localhost:8080/gen
- tail logs (kubectl): kubectl -n serving-runtime logs -l app=rt --since=2h | grep "kv_lock" > kv_lock_tail.log

Open questions to ask on triage channel:
- Has anyone else seen p99 regressions tied to eviction TTLs? (ping @sre)
- Are there recent changes to the eviction codepath (past 3 weeks) besides the micro-batcher PR?
- Ops: is +12% mem per pool acceptable short-term given our current reserved capacity?

Followups I will do tomorrow (prioritized):
1) Harden the synthetic (sequence permutations) so unit test can hit the hot-prefix + concurrent eviction pattern.
2) Prototype per-pool TTL override via runtime flag and run an A/B (50/50) for 4h.
3) Draft bug with timeline, PRs, and metrics — include suggested mitigations (revert, TTL bump, prefetch heuristic).

Slack snippets to copy into bug/PR description:
- "Observed p99 climb after micro-batcher rollout; traces show KV lock holds during eviction cycles. Reverting micro-batcher reduces tail immediately. Attaching traces and quick repro steps."

Small brain dump (save for later):
- Could be related to the new batching window heuristic that batches based on token arrival time rather than request-affinity; maybe a hybrid strategy (affinity-weighted windows) reduces cross-request KV touch.

End of note. Keep this doc as ephemeral working-log; will collate into RT-4312 if revert/patch confirmed.

-- Ling
